apiMessages.content: Plan my first 3 weeks back in the gym. Schedule all the sessions.

content.text: Reintroduction plan after 2 months off: ramping volume, not jumping to old loads. Week 1 = 3x full-body (reacquaint movement patterns, RPE 6-7, light loads). Weeks 2–3 = 4x/week upper/lower split, intensity climbing toward RPE 8 but still submaximal — don't chase old numbers yet, chase clean reps first.

apiMessages.content:
All 11 sessions scheduled, Sept 22 – Oct 10:

**Week 1 (full body x3):** Tue 9/22, Thu 9/24, Sat 9/26 — RPE 6-7, ~55-60% old loads. Rebuild patterns, not numbers.

**Week 2 (upper/lower x4):** Mon 9/28, Wed 9/30, Fri 10/2, Sat 10/3 — RPE 7, squat ~65%.

**Week 3 (upper/lower x4):** Mon 10/5, Wed 10/7, Fri 10/9, Sat 10/10 — RPE 8, squat ~75-80%, weighted pull-ups reintroduced.

Rules: hit prescribed reps clean before adding load — don't grind. If any session leaves you sore into the next one, that's the volume signal, not a reason to skip loading. If squat at 75-80% in week 3 feels like a genuine grind (not RPE 8), stop the ramp and hold there — that's real data on where you are, and week 4 planning should key off it.
Continue what — extend the block into week 4+, add nutrition logging, or something else? Say the word.
